If those 400 metrics are indeed ephemeral then this is a problem for the metadata footprint, and as a result a problem for agent start-up. It's also a problem for memory footprint because those dimensions will be kept in memory.

This was side effect of the changes we made on #9549, I fixed with the last commit.

> If those 400 metrics are indeed ephemeral

Why do i say that. Dimension is a combination of `ip` and `port`, it is clear that number of such combinations is huge. `Network viewer` adds to charts **first** N combinations, so it is likely we will have different set on every restart. New 400 on restart is worst case scenario, but it doesnt really matter because if it less (real case) it only makes _memory leak_ slower.

issue_context.title: Network Viewer Charts MVP0
issue_context.body:
##### Feature idea summary

We need to bring the following new charts as MVP0 of the Network Viewer:

 - ebpf.outbound_bytes:
     - `<port|service name>:<protocol>:<ip|hostname>_sent`
     - `<port|service name>:<protocol>:<ip|hostname>_received`
     - `other_sent`
     - `other_received`
   - ebpf.outbound_packets:
      - `<port|service name>:<protocol>:<ip|hostname>_sent`
      - `<port|service name>:<protocol>:<ip|hostname>_received`
     -  `other_sent`
     -  `other_received`
  - ebpf.outbound_retransmits:  `<port>:<protocol>:<ip>`
     -  ebpf.inbound_bytes:
        - `<port|service name>:<protocol>_sent`
        - `<port|service name>:<protocol>_received`
        - `other_sent`
         - `other_received`
  - ebpf.inbound_packets
     - `<port|service name>:<protocol>_sent`
     - `<port|service name>:<protocol>_received`
     - `other_sent`
     - `other_received`

##### Expected behavior

review_comments: `bytes/s` are reclassified to `kbyte/s` or another dimension when it i necessary. I think I did not understand your question.
